reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read all six scenes, five vocabulary entries, the pause question, two discussion questions, alt texts, content note, provenance and adaptation changes in full against the full rendered Ryder text on Wikisource, and re-read and approved the corrected text.

Two blockers fixed before approval: adaptation.changes now truthfully record that the source crow carries the mouse in its beak (here on its back, so the picture does not look like predation) and no longer claim the reunion was added; the scolding of the turtle is spoken by the mouse, as in the source.

Cause and effect follow Ryder: the crow finds the snared deer and brings the mouse, the mouse gnaws the snare, the turtle arrives out of love and is warned, the hunter takes the turtle tied to his bow, the mouse plans the pretend-dead deer, the hunter drops the turtle, the mouse frees it, all four escape and meet again. The pause question precedes the plan.
Violence softened and disclosed: no eye-pecking and no club. Content note truthful; narration neuter apart from the accepted idiom in the scene 6 title; no em dashes.
illustrations: Six equal 512px panels; vertical seams exactly at x=512; horizontal seams about 1px high (y=511/1023), invisible at display size; no faded borders after the edit pass.
Four friends consistent across panels: spotted chital, grey-necked crow, pink-eared mouse, domed olive turtle; the deer is largest.

Brown rope continuity: snare on the deer's leg in panels 2 and 3, tied to the turtle on the hunter's bow in panels 4 and 5, cut pieces in the grass in panel 6. Panel 2 shows the mouse riding on the flying crow's back.

The hunter is shown respectfully, from behind or at a distance, in plain cloth and headwrap; the bow is only carried, never aimed; no arrows or other weapons. One edit pass turned him toward the deer in panel 5.
Panel 5: the deer lies still with eyes closed, pretending, uninjured, while the mouse gnaws the turtle's rope. Panel 6: an evening reunion at the same lake, everyone unharmed.
Accepted minor issues: the deer lacks antlers in panel 5, the snared leg shifts from hind to front between panels 2 and 3, and the mouse and turtle are a little large relative to the crow.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age suitability has not been tested with children.

Source fidelity was checked against the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension; the Kannada character names were not checked against a Sanskrit edition.
Art was judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops; the coordinator checked the scenes load in the app at phone width, but not every scene in dark mode.
